speaker: Janae Rivers
cascadeSummary: I am holding the apprenticeship pipeline's disposition to the actual publication of the placement-gap analysis this cycle — West Oakland and Fruitvale named, owned, and dated — and I say plainly that the Fruitvale briefing record and the long-incomplete D5 audit must land on the public record before alternative response takes another step. Today I also put East Oakland's unanswered complaint on the Council response crosswalk with a named office and a next date, because my district gets answers, not patience. I vote YES on the Grand Lake proposal only with the Chen-Vega milestones and audit conditions intact, and I will not have the Mayor's office move faster on expansion than it moves on documentation.

statements.topic: Oakland Alternative Response Initiative — briefing record and expansion hold
statements.decision: Hold expansion until the D3 Fruitvale briefing record is executed and published with district-level and Fruitvale data, community participation documented, and responsible next dates filed for the still-incomplete D5 audit and Baylight feasibility review.
statements.quote: East Oakland's calls are already in this program — so East Oakland's record and Fruitvale's record get published before this program expands one block.
statements.fullStatement: I represent the district where alternative response already runs. The dispatch protocol is deployed, the calls are answered, and the promise was that residents who call 911 see their own record, in their own neighborhood, before the program grows. So I hold expansion. The D3 Fruitvale briefing record gets executed and published this cycle with district-level and Fruitvale data and documented community participation. The D5 audit that has been outstanding — and the Baylight feasibility review — come back with responsible offices and next dates, not another cycle of silence. I am not slowing this program because I want it smaller. I am slowing it until it can prove it is reaching people fairly, because expanding on a story instead of a record is how communities get skipped.

statements.topic: Oakland Youth Apprenticeship Pipeline — placement-gap analysis publication and disposition
statements.decision: Require publication this cycle of the placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan with explicit West Oakland and Fruitvale reviews, named placement reach, specific corrections, responsible owners, and next reporting dates — then set a binary disposition on the hearing agenda: evidence-supported advancement or recorded fail.
statements.quote: We handed East Oakland's youth the first rung. Now the ladder has to reach West Oakland and Fruitvale in a document the public can open, or we record the failure and try again in the open.
statements.fullStatement: I led on this pipeline because East Oakland's young people have been handed a first rung and told the ladder goes up. Four cycles in the same stage is not accountability — it is a filing cabinet. This cycle the placement-gap analysis and adjustment plan get published, with West Oakland and Fruitvale reviewed by name, who placements actually reach, the specific intake and placement corrections, the office that owns each one, and the next reporting date. Then this hearing ends in a disposition: evidence that supports advancing, or a recorded fail on the record. I support the Mayor's binary disposition because a program that serves young people owes them a verdict, not an automatic hold. The low-severity improvement flags are noted; they are not a finished analysis, and I will not represent them as one.

statements.topic: D5 constituent complaint — public response and next date
statements.decision: Place the unresolved D5 constituent complaint on the Mayor's ten-complaint response crosswalk with covered complaint ID, responsible office, proposed remedy, and next date, and hold the record until the Clerk supplies verified references rather than asserting docket numbers.
statements.quote: One unanswered complaint is one neighbor we told to wait — and I am done telling East Oakland to wait.
statements.fullStatement: My district has a complaint that went unresolved, and the public deserves to see it handled like any other on the ledger. I am asking that it appear on the complaint crosswalk with its covered ID, the responsible office that owes the remedy, the proposed fix, and the next date — so a neighbor can check the line rather than take my word for it. I also accept the discipline the Mayor applied to INIT-014: a response is not a resolution and a filing claim is not a Clerk entry without evidence, so the covered complaints get named, the uncovered ones get status, and the record waits for the Clerk's verified reference. I am not trading the integrity of this crosswalk for speed. East Oakland gets both: answers with dates, and answers that are true.

statements.topic: Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake — recorded full-council decision
statements.decision: Vote YES on the $2.5 million Grand Lake proposal with all Chen-Vega milestones and audit conditions remaining attached, and ask the Clerk to certify the roll call without forecasting the outcome.
statements.quote: Yes on Grand Lake — and yes with the receipts attached, not the conditions stripped.
statements.fullStatement: I vote yes on Grand Lake, and I say it the same way I said it last cycle: yes with the Chen-Vega milestones and audit conditions written into the result, not appended afterward by letter. A $2.5 million investment in commercial stabilization earns my vote when the public can follow the milestones and audit the spending, and when this body's decision lives in the Clerk's roll call rather than in a press release. I do not forecast the tally and I do not speak for the other eight seats. I put my name, and D5's vote, on the record as one member of nine, and I ask the Clerk to certify it so residents can read it for themselves.

statements.topic: Neighborhood conditions and civic life — East Oakland follow-through
statements.decision: Press responsible departments for public status on the reported service conditions, support direct listening in the north-end neighborhoods, and protect East Oakland's low crime as a result to defend rather than a budget line to absorb.
statements.quote: East Oakland's low crime is a result to protect, not a budget cut to absorb — and I will not treat our streets as the place where the city saves money.
statements.fullStatement: The report from my district says what residents already know: the mood has lifted, street trade is steady, crime is low. That is a result, and results have to be defended in a budget season and through every service map this Council touches. I keep pressing for public status from the responsible departments on the medium-severity spikes reported elsewhere — Glenview's public works and Piedmont Avenue's health — because that is what responsive government looks like, not a directive to invent an emergency. And I want room for neighborhoods to gather: the Mayor's mention of three block parties is the part of city life I will fight for. My district's work this cycle is follow-through, and I will keep asking the department that owes a date for the date.
